column1: # 218e pitch-CV calibration — the voltage the 208 needs at each pitch.
# MEASURED ON ONE SPECIFIC INSTRUMENT, WITH ITS 208 SET TO 1 V/OCTAVE.
# Both halves of that matter.  A tracking-error curve belongs to the oscillator
# it was measured from, so another 208 needs its own.  And it was taken with
# that 208 trimmed to 1 V/oct, which is not the [options].volts_per_octave
# default of 1.2 — the standard Buchla scaling that most instruments run.  At a
# different scaling the oscillator sits at a different operating point and its
# error curve is not the same one.
# So this file is an example and a record, not a starting point: measure your
# own, at the scaling you actually use.  That is why [options].pitch_correction
# is false by default.
# Offset_Cents is the only column the build reads: how far the output is
# pushed from an ideal 1 V/octave ramp, in cents of that ramp.  Positive
# raises the pitch.  Semitone 0 is the 208's 0 V pitch, an A
# key of the keyboard is semitone 3 (a C), shown in the Key column.
# Source:  octave       — from the octave calibration only, below the first key
#          measured     — a key you measured with a tuner
#          extrapolated — beyond the last measured key, holding its correction
# To recalibrate: measure the error of each key in cents (positive = sharp)
# and run  tools/build.py --fold-measurement <your.csv>  — it converts and
# folds the readings into this table, which is cumulative.
Semitone
